terms.long: IRE 1949 (as used in Weis & Gaylord 1985), IRE 1958 (as cited in Volk & Wöhlecke 2009) and IEEE Std 176-1987 (positive d33: tension along Z makes the +Z face positive) give the same +z for LN. The pyroelectric coefficient p3 is negative in this frame. Flipping +z (a 180 deg rotation about x) reverses every odd-rank tensor (e, d, r, chi(2), p3) but leaves the elastic and photoelastic tensors unchanged.
terms.short: The +z (+c) face of LiNbO3 is the c face that becomes negatively charged under compression along c and positively charged on cooling.

terms.long: The point group fixes which tensor components can be nonzero, for example the r tensor with independent r13, r22, r33 and r51. It lacks an inversion center, which allows piezoelectric, Pockels and chi(2) effects, and it is polar (the two ends of the threefold axis are inequivalent), which allows pyroelectricity. Weis & Gaylord 1985 prints the Schoenflies symbol as C6v, a typo; 3m corresponds to C3v. IEEE Std 176-1987 lists LiNbO3 as its example of class 3m.
terms.short: 3m (Schoenflies C3v) is the point group of ferroelectric LiNbO3: a threefold rotation axis along c with three mirror planes that contain it.

terms.long: Diffraction efficiency scales with the figure of merit M2 = n^6 p² / (rho v³); Weis & Gaylord 1985 tabulates acousto-optic figures of merit for LN. In thin-film LN, acoustic resonators and waveguides give GHz acousto-optic modulators and microwave-to-optical converters (Shao et al. 2019; Sarabalis & et al. 2020).
terms.short: The acousto-optic effect is the modulation or diffraction of light by an acoustic wave through the index changes it carries: photoelastic, plus electro-optic from the accompanying piezoelectric field in LiNbO3.

terms.long: In negative uniaxial LN, type-I SHG converts an o-polarized fundamental into an e-polarized harmonic. Angle tuning (critical phase matching) incurs walk-off; at theta = 90 deg, temperature tuning gives noncritical phase matching without walk-off (Miller et al. 1965). Because n_e depends on temperature and Li content, the matching temperature shifts with composition.
terms.short: Birefringent phase matching cancels material dispersion with the difference between ordinary and extraordinary indices, so that orthogonally polarized waves share the same phase velocity.

terms.long: Hirohashi et al. 2007 measured picosecond BLIIRA in single-domain and periodically poled ferroelectrics and found it lowest in KNbO3 and MgO:LN, and slightly increased by periodic poling. Like GRIIRA, it adds infrared absorption and heating that degrade high-power frequency conversion.
terms.short: BLIIRA is the infrared absorption induced in LiNbO3 by blue (or two-photon) excitation through the same light-generated polaron absorption bands.

terms.long: Unless grown at the congruent composition, a boule changes composition along its length as the melt drifts (Carruthers et al. 1971). Composition-sensitive quantities such as the Curie temperature or the UV absorption edge are used to check uniformity.
terms.short: A boule is the as-grown single-crystal ingot from which LiNbO3 wafers are cut after orientation.

terms.long: Glass et al. 1974 identified it as the driver of photorefraction in LN: in an open-circuit crystal, charge accumulates until conduction balances the current, giving E_sc ~ j_pv / (sigma_d + sigma_ph), which is large in insulating crystals. terms.short: The bulk photovoltaic effect is a DC current driven by uniform illumination in a crystal without inversion symmetry, j = kappa alpha I along c in LiNbO3, with no applied field or gradient.

terms.short: A clamped coefficient (superscript S) is defined at constant strain, the condition reached at drive frequencies above the mechanical resonances of the sample, where the lattice cannot follow the field.

terms.long: Clamped (constant strain, S): field frequency above mechanical resonances. Free (constant stress, T): includes the indirect contribution through converse piezoelectric strain and photoelasticity, r^T = r^S + p d.

terms.short: A traveling-wave electrode is a transmission line running along the optical waveguide so that the modulating microwave co-propagates with the light, removing the RC limit of a lumped electrode.

Definitions differ (single arm or push-pull, DC or RF, wavelength), so published values are not strictly comparable. Narrower gaps lower V_pi*L but raise optical loss from the metal.
terms.short: V_pi*L is the product of half-wave voltage and electrode length, a length-independent figure of merit for electro-optic modulation efficiency, usually in V cm.

terms.short: Vapor transport equilibration (VTE) raises the Li content of LiNbO3 wafers toward stoichiometry by annealing them next to Li-rich powder so that Li2O diffuses in through the vapor phase.

terms.long: For a lossless traveling-wave modulator with mismatch Delta n = n_m - n_g, the response follows |sin(x)/x| with x = pi f L Delta n / c, which bounds the product f L. In bulk LN the microwave index far exceeds the optical group index, while TFLN on low-permittivity substrates can bring the two close.
terms.short: Velocity matching equalizes the microwave phase velocity on the electrode (index n_m) with the optical group velocity (index n_g), so the light sees the same modulating phase along the whole device.

terms.short: Wafer bonding joins two polished wafers, for example an implanted LiNbO3 donor and an oxidized Si or LN handle, by direct or adhesive bonding.

terms.long: For propagation at angle theta to the optic axis, tan(rho) = (n(theta)² / 2) |1/n_e² - 1/n_o²| sin(2 theta), which vanishes at theta = 0 and 90 deg. This is why noncritical (90 deg) phase matching in LN avoids walk-off (Miller et al. 1965), as does QPM along a principal axis.
terms.short: Walk-off is the angle rho between the Poynting vector and the wave vector of an extraordinary wave in a birefringent crystal, which separates beams and limits the useful interaction length.

terms.long: In X-cut TFLN, coplanar electrodes on both sides of a waveguide apply an in-plane field along z, and a TE mode polarized along z uses n_e and r33; this is the common TFLN modulator geometry. Periodic poling of X-cut films also uses coplanar electrodes, which give a field that is nonuniform in depth.
terms.short: An X-cut LiNbO3 wafer or film has its surface normal along the crystal x axis, so the c axis lies in the plane.

terms.long: Wafer named after the crystal axis normal to its surface. x-cut TFLN puts Z in plane so TE modes use r33 [Wang et al. 2018; P].
terms.short: Wafer named after the crystal axis normal to its surface.

terms.long: The resonance is set mainly by plate thickness rather than electrode pitch, which allows GHz operation with relaxed lithography; Plessky et al. 2019 reported 5 GHz XBARs on thin LN platelets. Thin-film LN resonators of this class are being extended to mm-wave filters (Lu 2025).
terms.short: An XBAR is a suspended thin LiNbO3 plate with interdigital electrodes on its surface whose lateral field excites a thickness-shear bulk mode.

terms.long: The rotation angle selects the velocity, coupling and spurious responses of acoustic waves on the plate. Shibayama et al. 1976 identified a rotated Y-cut near 128 deg with X propagation as optimum for surface-acoustic-wave filter substrates.
terms.short: A Y-cut LiNbO3 wafer has its surface normal along the crystal y axis, which lies in a mirror plane; a rotated Y-cut tilts that normal about x by a stated angle.

terms.long: In Z-cut TFLN a vertical field couples to TM-like modes through r33, while TE modes see n_o and smaller coefficients. Poling is done with a field through the film or by poling a bulk wafer before bonding. A temperature change leaves pyroelectric charge on the faces, producing a vertical field that overlaps strongly with the mode.
terms.short: A Z-cut LiNbO3 wafer or film has its surface normal along the polar c axis, so its two faces are the +z and -z faces.
